column1: # Forage reviewed supplement to Unicode TR39 confusables (owner ruling, 2026-10-06).
# TR39 maps many look-alikes to a non-ASCII "prototype" (for example Cyrillic
# U+043A to U+0138 KRA), which the generator drops: a fold must end in ASCII.
# Each row below names the Latin letter a reader sees instead. The generator
# merges these after TR39 (a row wins over a TR39 mapping of the same source)
# and refuses a row whose target is non-ASCII, whose source is ASCII, or whose
# Format: U+XXXX<TAB>latin<TAB>reason. Lines starting with '#' and blank lines
# are ignored. Every row was checked against the `multilingual` benign genre:
# folding that genre's records moves no stage-2 verdict (see

column3: CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER KA reads as k
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER TE reads as a small-cap t
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER PE reads as n
CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER PE reads as a wide N
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER EM reads as a small-cap m
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER I is a mirrored n
CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER I is a mirrored N
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER EN reads as a small-cap h
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER DE reads as g in many typefaces
CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER DE reads as g in many typefaces
CYRILLIC SMALL LETTER EL reads as a flat-topped n
CYRILLIC CAPITAL LETTER EL reads as a flat-topped N
GREEK SMALL LETTER KAPPA reads as k
GREEK SMALL LETTER TAU reads as t
GREEK SMALL LETTER ETA reads as n
GREEK SMALL LETTER MU reads as u
GREEK SMALL LETTER EPSILON reads as e
GREEK SMALL LETTER BETA reads as b
GREEK SMALL LETTER PI reads as n
GREEK CAPITAL LETTER PI reads as a wide N
GREEK SMALL LETTER CHI reads as x
